n: A song of Zion celebrating God’s victory over an enemy army. God has made himself known in Judah, and his name is great in Israel. Many link it with the defeat of Assyria in Hezekiah’s day.
His tent is in Salem — an old name for Jerusalem — and his dwelling in Zion.

f.g: An ancient name for Jerusalem, where Melchizedek was king.
Literally “lair” or “booth” — continuing the lion imagery.

n: There God shattered the enemy’s flaming arrows, shields and swords — he ended the war itself.

f.g: Literally “the flashes of the bow” — fiery arrows.

n: God is radiant and majestic — greater than the mountains where predators hunt their prey.

f.g: Mountains full of game — or the enemy’s mountain strongholds.

n: The bravest warriors were plundered; they fell into the sleep of death and couldn’t lift a hand.
At God’s rebuke, horses and chariot riders were stunned into deathly sleep.
God alone is to be reverenced. Who can stand before him when he is angry?

f.w: who may stand in thy sight

n: God pronounced judgment from heaven, and the earth fell silent in awe.
He rose to judge in order to save all the humble of the earth. God’s judgment is for rescue.
Even human fury ends up bringing God praise, and he restrains whatever wrath remains. God can turn even opposition to his purposes.

f.w: the wrath of man shall praise thee

n: Make vows to the Lord and keep them; let the surrounding nations bring gifts to the one who deserves reverence.
God humbles the pride of princes and is awesome to the kings of the earth.

f.w: cut off the spirit of princes
